question: If a file has the same contents in two consecutive Git snapshots, how does Git avoid storing a second copy?
expected_answer: It reuses the stored identical file by reference.
evidence_quote: To be efficient, if files have not changed, Git doesn't store the file again, just a link to the previous identical file it has already stored.

question: I am configuring Git for the first time. When a system-wide setting and this repository's own setting disagree, which one wins?
expected_answer: The setting in the repository's .git/config overrides the system-wide value.
evidence_quote: Each level overrides values in the previous level, so values in `.git/config` trump those in `[path]/etc/gitconfig`.

question: In a centralized version-control system, what is left of the project history if the central database disk fails and no backups exist?
expected_answer: The history is lost except for the individual snapshots users happen to have locally.
evidence_quote: If the hard disk the central database is on becomes corrupted, and proper backups haven't been kept, you lose absolutely everything -- the entire history of the project except whatever single snapshots people happen to have on their local machines.

question: How can I choose a different local folder name when cloning a Git repository?

question: What character do I put at the beginning of a .gitignore pattern to negate it?
expected_answer: An exclamation mark (!).
evidence_quote: You can negate a pattern by starting it with an exclamation point (`!`).

question: In Git Basics, does downloading remote updates with git fetch immediately merge those updates into my current work?
expected_answer: No. git fetch downloads the data to the local repository without merging it or modifying the current work.
evidence_quote: It's important to note that the `git fetch` command only downloads the data to your local repository -- it doesn't automatically merge it with any of your work or modify what you're currently working on.

question: How do I push only annotated tags to a remote while leaving lightweight tags local?
expected_answer: Use git push <remote> --follow-tags.
evidence_quote: if you use `git push <remote> --follow-tags` only annotated tags will be pushed to the remote.

question: When one branch tip is directly ahead of the current commit with no divergent work, what happens to the current pointer during the merge?
expected_answer: Git moves the current branch pointer forward to the merged tip in a fast-forward.
evidence_quote: when you try to merge one commit with a commit that can be reached by following the first commit's history, Git simplifies things by moving the pointer forward because there is no divergent work to merge together

question: I created a branch using git branch and then kept working. Did the command also check out the new branch for me?
expected_answer: No. git branch creates the branch and leaves the current branch checked out.
evidence_quote: The `git branch` command only _created_ a new branch -- it didn't switch to that branch.

question: When does the book warn against rebasing commits that I have shared with teammates?
expected_answer: Avoid rebasing commits that already exist outside the local repository and that other people may have based work on.
evidence_quote: Do not rebase commits that exist outside your repository and that people may have based work on.

question: How can a Git stash include files that are explicitly ignored as well as untracked files?
expected_answer: Use git stash --all or its short form -a.
evidence_quote: However, including untracked files in the stash will still not include explicitly _ignored_ files; to additionally include ignored files, use `--all` (or just `-a`).

question: In Git revision syntax, what does d921970^2 refer to?
expected_answer: The second parent of commit d921970.
evidence_quote: `d921970^2` means "`the second parent of d921970.`"

question: In the Git Tools chapter, which git grep option shows the surrounding function or method for each matching string?
expected_answer: Use -p or --show-function.

question: Will a fresh clone automatically install the client-side Git hooks from the original repository?
expected_answer: No. Client-side hooks are not copied by git clone.
evidence_quote: It's important to note that client-side hooks are *not* copied when you clone a repository.

question: If I set GIT_DIR but leave every work-tree override unset, where does Git treat the top of the working tree as being?
expected_answer: The current working directory is treated as the root of the working tree.
evidence_quote: If `--git-dir` or `GIT_DIR` is specified but none of `--work-tree`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` or `core.worktree` is specified, the current working directory is regarded as the top level of your working tree.

question: My last commit is already on the shared server. Does the book recommend amending it to add a missed change?
expected_answer: No. It recommends amending only commits that are still local and have never been pushed.
evidence_quote: Only amend commits that are still local and have not been pushed somewhere.

question: While working through Git Branching, I finished a feature and want to remove its branch from the shared server. Which git push option removes it?
expected_answer: Use the --delete option with the remote and branch name, for example git push origin --delete serverfix.
evidence_quote: You can delete a remote branch using the `--delete` option to `git push`.

question: What Git feature can remember my manual resolution of a merge conflict and reuse it when the same conflict happens again?
expected_answer: git rerere, short for reuse recorded resolution.
evidence_quote: The `git rerere` functionality is a bit of a hidden feature. The name stands for "`reuse recorded resolution`" and, as the name implies, it allows you to ask Git to remember how you've resolved a hunk conflict so that the next time it sees the same conflict, Git can resolve it for you automatically.

question: How can I keep a tracked directory in the project but omit it from an archive made with git archive?
expected_answer: Set the export-ignore attribute for the path in the Git attributes file.
evidence_quote: If there is a subdirectory or file that you don't want to include in your archive file but that you do want checked into your project, you can determine those files via the `export-ignore` attribute.

question: In the book's two-version packfile example, which version is stored in full and why?
expected_answer: The second, newer version is stored in full to speed access to the version likely to be needed most. The original is stored as a delta.
evidence_quote: What is also interesting is that the second version of the file is the one that is stored intact, whereas the original version is stored as a delta -- this is because you're most likely to need faster access to the most recent version of the file.
